Consult Summary:
27-year-old male with 3-day history of profuse watery diarrhoea, abdominal cramping, nausea/vomiting, and subjective fever, likely viral gastroenteritis. Provided hydration, diet, and OTC oral rehydration advice; safety-net to call back within 48 h if no improvement.

Problem List:

Issue 1: Acute watery diarrhoea with dehydration risk
- Onset 3 days ago; loose, watery stools “almost every hour” while awake.
- Associated symptoms: crampy mid-lower abdominal pain (intermittent, ~6/10), nausea, occasional vomiting (worse with milk), subjective fever, reduced urine frequency.
- Denies blood in stool.
- Brother with similar illness ×5 days (possible infectious contact).
- No current red-flag features (no persistent vomiting, no hematochezia, no severe constant pain).
- Impression: Likely infectious gastroenteritis.

Issue 2: Dehydration / fluid-electrolyte loss
- High stool frequency and vomiting → risk of dehydration; patient reports fluids “going straight through”.
- Subjective feeling of being “very hot”; taking paracetamol ad-hoc.

Issue 3: Family history of colorectal cancer
- Father with stage III colon cancer (timing unspecified).

Medications:
- Paracetamol (dose/route/frequency not documented).
- OTC oral rehydration solution (Dioralyte) advised – not yet commenced.

Allergies:
- No known drug allergies.

Past Medical History:
- Denies chronic illnesses; otherwise fit and well.

Social History:
- Lives with mother and sister; brother lives separately.
- Occupation: Government office worker in Central London.
- Smoking: Occasional social smoker (a few cigarettes, mainly on Fridays).
- Alcohol: 1 beer on some weekdays; heavier drinking sessions once or twice per month.
- No illicit drug use mentioned.

Preventative History:
- No information provided regarding screening tests or vaccinations.

Physical Examination:
- No vitals or physical findings documented (consult conducted by video).

Plan:
- Diagnosis: Probable viral gastroenteritis.
- Hydration: Encourage clear fluids; start oral rehydration salts (Dioralyte) per package instructions.
- Diet: Soft/bland foods (soups, mashed foods) as tolerated; advance diet gradually.
- Medications: Continue paracetamol for fever/pain as needed; avoid alcohol.
- Red-flag advice: Seek review or ED care if unable to keep fluids down, decreased urine output, persistent fever, blood in stool, worsening pain, or no improvement within 48 h.
- Follow-up: Telephone review in 48 h if symptoms not settling.

Quality checks (document_quality):
● Missing expected elements: No vitals, no abdominal or general physical examination findings, no formal medication reconciliation beyond paracetamol.  
● Internal conflicts: None noted.  
● Transcript quality: Clear; minor interruptions but clinically adequate information gathered.
